title: Chapter 15 — Ventilation
intro: The most under-sold category — CFM pairing, duct reality, hood types, and the system sale.

sections.title: The Most Under-Sold Category
sections.content:
Ventilation is where money gets left on the table. Most salespeople sell the range and forget the hood. But proper ventilation is not optional — it is required by building codes when cooking appliance BTUs exceed certain thresholds.

Every range sale should include a ventilation conversation. That is not upselling. That is completing the system.

sections.title: CFM Pairing
sections.content:
Hood CFM must match the cooktop's output. The general rule: 1 CFM per 100 BTU for gas ranges. A 60,000 BTU range needs at minimum a 600 CFM hood.

Under-speccing ventilation creates smoke, grease, and odour problems. Over-speccing wastes money and can create negative pressure issues. Know the math.

sections.title: Duct Reality
sections.content:
Ductwork is the hidden factor. Many customers assume their kitchen is set up for a hood — but existing ductwork may be undersized, routed poorly, or nonexistent.

Recirculating hoods are an alternative when ductwork is not feasible — but they do not perform at the same level. Be honest about the trade-offs.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating ventilation knowledge, ask:

Does the salesperson include ventilation in every cooking sale?
Can they calculate CFM requirements based on cooktop BTU?
Do they discuss ductwork realities honestly — including recirculating limitations?
Do they treat ventilation as part of the cooking system — not an afterthought?
